narration: Every free sample you've ever accepted? That wasn't generosity. It was neuroscience — and it's quietly costing you $1,800 a year. Here's how.
visual: Animated arm extending upward holding a small sample cup. 'FREE SAMPLE' stat text appears. Three dollar signs drift upward and to the right. Stats at bottom: '$1,800 per year' fades in.

narration: It's called the Reciprocity Principle. When someone gives you something, your brain fires an overwhelming urge to give back — even if you never asked for the gift.
visual: Head/brain icon springs into frame. Three-step flow appears in sequence: green 'GIFT' box → red 'OBLIGATION' box → amber 'BUY' box. 'THE RECIPROCITY TRAP' stamps in at bottom.

narration: Costco's sample stations boost purchase rates by up to 300 percent for that item. One study tracked a single demo station generating $1.8 million in extra sales. That's not a snack — that's a sales machine.
visual: Warehouse store with shelves and products animates in. Sample station visible at bottom. Counter counts from 0 to 300, then '%' pops in. 'MORE SALES' label below.

narration: Wine stores, food courts, grocery demos — the reciprocity trigger is everywhere. And the average impulse purchase that follows a free taste runs about $47. Next scene has the real damage.
visual: Wine bottle springs in on left side. Sample tray with small cups rises on right side. Large '$47' slams in below center. 'TRIGGERED PER SAMPLE' label below.

narration: Add it up — Costco runs, grocery demos, wine tastings, food hall stops — and the average family spends $1,800 extra per year on purchases they never planned to make.
visual: Person silhouette with arms out. Dollar signs float upward away from them. Counter animates from $0 to $1,800. '/YEAR DRAINED' label beneath the counter.

narration: Here's the fix. Go ahead, accept the sample — they're delicious. But pause before you buy anything and ask one question: did I plan this? That one second saves you $1,800 a year. Follow for more.
visual: Shield with checkmark springs in. Three numbered steps appear in sequence: 'Accept the sample', 'Pause before buying', 'Ask: Did I plan this?'. Dark CTA box slides up at bottom: '$1,800 SAVED'.
